question: Is the provider-contract evidence sufficient to land these seven server and recorder behavior changes together, or should the highest-risk compatibility and delivery changes be split or independently proven?
rationale: Repository policy requires provider-native fidelity, while the branch changes several externally observable contracts and retry boundaries in one patch; accepting that evidence and breadth requires human judgment.

options.title: Require representative provider proof
options.body: Keep the combined PR but require authoritative contract references or representative compatible-client runs for the changed authentication, identity, ordering, and error behavior.

options.title: Split high-risk surfaces
options.body: Land independently reviewable HTTP and provider fixes separately from recorder, shutdown, and delivery-order changes.

options.title: Accept focused tests
options.body: Merge the combined hardening based on the successful focused suite and repository-member ownership of the patch.

recommendation.title: Require representative provider proof
recommendation.body: Keep the combined PR but require authoritative contract references or representative compatible-client runs for the changed authentication, identity, ordering, and error behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed repository member connected to the full cross-provider change set in the available review context.
